activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept and scope of economics (meaning and origin, importance, its relationship with other subjects, basic terminologies, branches, the central economic problem and fundamental economic questions)
suggested_methods: Role play: Guide students to create a list of wants and needs and use their classification rationale to relate to the concept and scope of economics

Jigsaw: Guide students to discuss meaning and origin, importance, its relationship with other subjects, basic terminologies, branches, central economic problem and fundamental economic questions in their local perspectives
The students present their findings, and the teacher relates those findings with the concept and scope of economics
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept and scope of economics is well described
suggested_resources: Bank of Tanzania (BOT) publication and reports
Tanzania Development Vision 2025 and Five-Year Development Plans

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (b)   Describe economic systems (forms, features, advantages and disadvantages)
suggested_methods: Project: In teams, students search for the different forms and features of economic systems, their advantages, and disadvantages
Discussion: Students discuss their findings and the teacher relate the students’ findings with the concept of economic system
activities.assessment_criteria: Economic systems are well described
suggested_resources: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) reports, working papers, and publications

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explore the basic tenets of microeconomics (meaning, scope and goals)
suggested_methods: Field trip: Students visit the nearby community and observe the prevailing economic activities, learn the way individual consumers, households, and firms make decisions, and then write the report on their observations
Discussion: Students share their experiences on the types, scopes and goals of the observed activities and present their findings
Teacher relates the students’ findings with the tenets of microeconomics
Project: Students apply tenets of micro-economics to choose a project for their club
activities.assessment_criteria: Basic tenets of microeconomics are well described

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (d)  Describe the price theory (demand, supply, market equilibrium and elasticity)
suggested_methods: Case study: Provide case studies portraying quantity demanded and quantity supplied of different commodities at different prices. Let the students discuss the questions related to demand, supply, market equilibrium, and elasticity
The teacher relates the discussion to the price theory
Project: Students use price theory to simulate their product/service price catalogue
activities.assessment_criteria: Price theory is well described

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (e)  Describe the theories of production and costs (factors of production,
suggested_methods: Guest speaker: Invite a businessperson to explain his/her production process in relation to resources use, costs, revenue and profits
activities.assessment_criteria: Theories of production and costs are well described
suggested_resources: Educational Videos related to production and cost

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: production function, objectives and profit of firms, scale and costs of production and revenue)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Students discuss their findings in relation to the factors of production, production function, objectives and profit of firms, scale and costs of production, and revenue
The teacher relates the discussion with the theories of production and costs
Project: Students write a one-page article/blog about the production process
activities.assessment_criteria: Theories of production and costs are well described

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (f) Describe the concept of the market (meaning, types and structures)
suggested_methods: Scenario: Prepare a scenario on the different types of market structures.
Project: Students use market concept to improve their simulated product/service price catalogue
activities.assessment_criteria: Concept of market is well described

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.2  Demonstrate mastery of economic analysis
activities.learning_activity: (a) Examine the influence of the economic system on resource allocation and distribution
suggested_methods: Scenario: Use a scenario to guide the students to examine how each economic system works in terms of resource allocation and distribution.
Discussion: Students discuss the economic systems and their applications locally and globally. Teachers relate the discussions with the economic systems and their applications
activities.assessment_criteria: Influence of economic systems on resource allocation and distribution is well examined
suggested_resources: The World Bank publication, reports and policy documents related to economic development in Tanzania

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.2  Demonstrate mastery of economic analysis
activities.learning_activity: (b) Use the price theory to explain the effects of pricing on consumer behaviour and business profits
suggested_methods: Case study: Use a case study to explore the effects of pricing on consumer behaviour and business profits
Discussion: Let the students discuss the questions related to the effects of pricing on consumer choice decisions and business profits. Teachers relate the discussions with the price theory
activities.assessment_criteria: Effects of pricing on consumer behaviour and business profits are well examined using price theory

activities.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.2  Demonstrate mastery of economic analysis
activities.learning_activity: (c) Apply production, cost and market theories to make decisions on price and output
suggested_methods: Case study: Provide a case study with information on various production, cost and revenue data of the business
Discussion: Allow students discuss the questions related to the production cost and pricing decisions of different types market’s theories
Project: Students create a market simulation game, where they act as buyers or sellers and make pricing and production decisions based on market conditions
activities.assessment_criteria: Production, cost, and market theories are well applied to make decisions on price and output

activities.main_competence: 2.0.  Conduct a project in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 2.1  Design and carry out a project in Economics
activities.learning_activity: (a) Design and execute a research project on an appropriate economic problem
suggested_methods: Thin-ink-pair-share: Students discuss the concept of economic research
Brainstorming: Guide students to identify and discuss economic problems that affect their surrounding communities
Project: Guide students in manageable groups, guide the students to develop a mini- proposal on the selected one of the economic variables
Project: Guide students to collect data on the identified economic issue and write a report
activities.assessment_criteria: Economic research is well described, A mini-research proposal on an economic issue is well designed, Data on the identified economic issue are well collected

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Explore the basic tenets of macroeconomics (meaning, scope and goals)
suggested_methods: Case study: Prepare a case study on the basic tenets of macroeconomics
activities.assessment_criteria: Basic tenets of macroeconomics are well described
suggested_resources: Bank of Tanzania (BOT) publication and reports
Tanzania Development Vision 2025 and Five- Year Development Plans

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Describe national income (key terms, approaches of measuring, determinants, importance, effect on standard of living and determination of equilibrium)
suggested_methods: Project: Allow the students to search National Income
Students write the reports and presents their findings
Teacher relates the students’ findings with the national income
activities.assessment_criteria: National income is well described
suggested_resources: Government Publications and Central Bank Reports

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Describe unemployment (key terms, forms, causes, effects and control measures)
suggested_methods: Scenario: Use a scenario to have students discuss key terms, forms, causes of unemployment
Have the students present their findings and teacher relates the findings with the concept of unemployment
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the effects, and control measures of unemployment
activities.assessment_criteria: Unemployment is well described
suggested_resources: Prime Minister’s Office Labour, Youth, Employment & Persons with Disability publications and reports

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Describe money (key terms, the evolution of money, functions and monetary policies)
suggested_methods: Scenario: Use a scenario to have students describe the concept of money
Teacher relates the findings from the discussion by relating with the key terms, the evolution of and functions of money, and monetary policies
activities.assessment_criteria: The Term Money is well described

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Describe inflation (meaning, types, causes, effects and control measures)
suggested_methods: Project: In teams, students visit nearby shops and search for information on the prices of different commodities in different periods of times and write a short report on their observations
Have the students present their reports and the teachers relate their presentation with the concept of inflation

Group Discussion: In groups, the students discuss the factors that might have caused the increase in price levels in their areas, the effects of increase in prices to their society and the measures to control
Have the students present their findings from the discussion
Teachers relate their presentation with the concept of inflation
activities.assessment_criteria: Inflation is well described
suggested_resources: Local Economic News Outlets: such as newspapers, magazines, and online news platforms

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Describe public finance (key terms, government revenue and expenditure, public debt and fiscal policy)
suggested_methods: Gallery walks: Guide students to explore different themes on key terms of public finance, government revenue and expenditure
Discussion: Let the students discuss the concept of public debt and fiscal policy
activities.assessment_criteria: Public finance is well described
suggested_resources: Ministry of Finance and Planning of Tanzania reports
Policy documents related to public finance

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Describe international trade (meaning, advantages, disadvantages, terms of trade, balance of payments, absolute and comparative advantage and protectionism)
suggested_methods: Discussion: students discuss the meaning of international trade together with its, advantages and disadvantages
Students present their findings Teacher relates the discussions with international trade
Project: In teams, students search for information on the terms of trade, balance of payments, absolute, and comparative advantage, and protectionism
Students present their findings Teacher relates the discussions with international trade
activities.assessment_criteria: International trade well described
suggested_resources: Tanzania trade policies, regulations, and initiatives
Tanzania Trade Development Authority (TanTrade): reports and resources on export promotion, market research and trade statistics
United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) reports and publications
World Trade Organization (WTO): publications policies, agreements, statistics and reports.
Economic and Social Research Foundation (ESRF) reports
Tanzania Chamber of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture (TCCIA) reports

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate mastery of economic analysis
activities.learning_activity: Apply macroeconomic theories to explain the state of national and international economies
suggested_methods: Project: Collect data on national income and international trade variables in different periods of time
Students describe the data and interpret the findings to show the state of national and international economies
Students present their findings Teacher relates the discussions from findings with macroeconomic theories
activities.assessment_criteria: Macroeconomic theories are well applied to explain the state of national and international economies
suggested_resources: The World Bank publication, reports and policy documents related to economic development

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate mastery of economic analysis
activities.learning_activity: Apply macroeconomic theories to explain the levels of socio-economic development of nations
suggested_methods: Case study: Use a case study to portray the levels of socio-economic development of nations
Have the students discuss the questions on the case studies Teacher relates the discussions with macroeconomic theories
activities.assessment_criteria: Macroeconomic theories to discuss the levels of socio-economic development of nations are well applied

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Conduct a project in Economics
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Design and carry out a project in Economics
activities.learning_activity: Complete and submit a report of the project developed in Form Five
suggested_methods: Project 1: Guide students to analyse and interpret data from project developed in Form Five and present the findings
Project 2: Guide students to write the report from project developed in Form Five
Discussion: Students present and discuss their project works developed in Form Five
Teacher relates students’ discussions with the execution of research project on an appropriate economic problem in society
Students submit their projects reports
activities.assessment_criteria: Simple software to analyse data collected in Form Five is well used
